claims.text: Redis documentation defines RDB as point-in-time snapshots, AOF as logging every write operation for replay at startup, no persistence, and combined RDB+AOF. It documents RDB's compact backup/disaster-recovery and faster-large-dataset restart advantages, and snapshot data-loss/fork-stall boundaries; it documents AOF size and fsync-policy tradeoffs and recommends using both methods when higher data safety is needed.

Redis documentation specifies appendfsync always/everysec/no behavior, says everysec is the suggested and default policy and may lose one second of data in a disaster, and documents background AOF rewrite while the old file continues receiving appends before switching to the new file.

Redis documentation states that Redis 7.0.0 introduced multi-part AOF with base and incremental files tracked by a manifest, documents its rewrite manifest replacement, and distinguishes truncated AOF recovery from invalid mid-file corruption and repair outcomes.

findings: 2026-07-11 核验的 Redis 官方 persistence 文档覆盖全部材料性主张，候选哈希与 evidence sidecar 一致。
答案按 concept 审查，覆盖 RDB/AOF 定义、统一比较、选型条件、关闭持久化边界、Redis 7.0.0 multi-part AOF 与配置敏感的 fsync/rewrite 细节。
